name: The Okafor Hour
description: A weekly underground mesh broadcast hosted by a figure known only as Okafor — believed to be a rotating collective of three to five hosts sharing the persona — that combines long-form interviews with Shelf community organizers, practical segments on corponation legal exposure and tenant rights, and a recurring feature called 'The Receipt,' in which documented evidence of corporate misconduct is read aloud in full without commentary. The broadcast deliberately uses a calm, unhurried register — no urgency, no fear — as a counter to what the hosts describe as 'the poverty of panic that passes for Shelf media.
cultural_impact: 'The Receipt' format — the slow, undramatic reading of documented evidence — was adopted by at least a dozen other underground outlets and became a signature genre of Shelf counter-media in the 2210s.
story_hooks: One of the rotating 'Okafor' hosts has been offered a substantial sum by an unknown party to identify the other hosts — and is trying to find out who's buying before deciding what to do.
The most recent 'Receipt' segment referenced a document that hasn't been publicly leaked yet — meaning someone inside a corponation is feeding the broadcast in real time.
A Tier 3 media executive has been quietly listening to The Okafor Hour for two years and is on the verge of making a decision that will either help the broadcast or destroy it.
